title: Hypoallergenicity of Hydrolyzed Rice Protein Formula in Children with Cow’s Milk Allergy
author: Zemrani, Boutaina
materials: Macronutrient and HMO composition of study formulas.

steps.title: Obtain consent, screen, and randomize
steps.instruction: After obtaining written informed consent, verify that the child (60 days–3 years) meets the IgE‑mediated CMA eligibility criteria and has no exclusion criteria, then randomize 1:1 to the sequence HRF‑HMO → AAF‑HMO or AAF‑HMO → HRF‑HMO using the Medidata Rave RTSM system.

steps.title: Prepare blinded study formulas
steps.instruction: A designated, non‑assessing staff reconstitutes each powder formula (HRF‑HMO and AAF‑HMO) with water, packages them in identical containers, affixes a unique code on the primary packaging, and records the code in the blinded system; HRF‑HMO contains hydrolyzed rice protein (2.3 g/100 kcal), 2’FL and LNnT at 1.5 g/L (2:1 ratio), medium‑chain triglycerides and meets arsenic limits; AAF‑HMO is the commercial amino‑acid formula (Alfamino HMO®, 2.67 g/100 kcal) with the same HMOs.

steps.title: Schedule challenge with health and wash‑out checks
steps.instruction: Plan the DBPCFC on a day when the child is healthy; postpone if the child is ill or has taken antihistamines within the previous 7 days or oral steroids within the previous 14 days.

steps.title: Give pre‑challenge feeding instructions
steps.instruction: Instruct parents to feed the child a light, non‑fatty meal equal to about half of the usual portion ~2 hours before the test, to avoid any food or drink after that meal until the challenge is finished, and to maintain a strict cow‑milk‑free diet throughout the study.

steps.title: Perform incremental formula feeding challenge
steps.instruction: Administer the assigned blinded formula in increasing volumes at intervals of ≥20 minutes until the age‑appropriate target volume is reached:

substeps.instruction: Measure vital signs and perform a brief physical exam before each dose.
Give the next dose (minimum total volume 180 mL up to 210 mL for infants <1 year; minimum 200 mL up to 240 mL for children ≥1 year).
If the child cannot finish the total volume, allow a short break and a re‑attempt, or reschedule the challenge at the investigator’s discretion.

steps.title: Observe and document reactions
steps.instruction: During the challenge, record any skin, gastrointestinal, respiratory, or cardiovascular symptoms on the standardized data‑collection form; after the final dose, keep the child under observation for a minimum of 2 hours.

steps.title: Determine pass/fail outcome
steps.instruction: Declare the challenge passed if the child consumes the full target volume without a dose‑limiting allergic reaction; declare it failed if a dose‑limiting reaction occurs; any inability to drink the full volume for non‑allergic reasons is recorded as an incomplete (not failed) challenge.

steps.title: Provide 7‑day open‑label home phase
steps.instruction: For children who pass both DBPCFCs, supply HRF‑HMO for 7 days at home with instructions to drink at least 240 mL daily (in one or multiple servings). Caregivers record daily formula intake, gastrointestinal symptoms (flatulence, vomiting, discomfort, stool frequency, stool consistency per Brussels Infant and Toddler Stool Scale), and any adverse events in a diary.

steps.title: Collect adverse‑event data throughout study
steps.instruction: From consent signing until the end of the home phase, investigators record type, severity, seriousness, duration, and relationship of all adverse events using MedDRA terminology; after the open‑label phase, parents may report events spontaneously during the optional 4‑month post‑study access period.
